final_text:
**The workspace was empty — no code, no query logs, no corpus — so I can't tell you why *your* results are irrelevant.** I won't guess at a cause; the value I can add is the method that localizes it, plus the specific inputs that would change the answer. Full write-up: [search-relevance-diagnosis.md](search-relevance-diagnosis.md).

**The key reframe:** "feels irrelevant" is a perception, not a measurement. It bundles at least five distinct failures, and they have *different fixes* — spending on a ranker when the real problem is a stale index or an unhighlighted snippet list is the standard way this project wastes a quarter.

**Diagnosis, in cost order:**

1. **Freeze a judgment set first** — 50–100 stratified real queries, graded 0–3 by 2–3 raters including the complainers. Until this exists, no change is falsifiable.
2. **Slice the logs before touching the ranker.** Reformulation rate (query edited within 30s) is the strongest "results were wrong" signal available; zero-result rate separates coverage gaps from matching failures; flat CTR across positions points at a presentation problem rather than relevance. One bucket usually accounts for 60–80% of complaints.
3. **One test per failure mode** — query understanding: re-run with a hand-normalized query; recall: is the known-good doc in the index, then in candidates *before* ranking; ranking: median rank of known-good items; presentation: same result set with better snippets, does the complaint persist. Presentation is often the cheapest fix with the largest perceived gain, so check it before buying a ranker.

**Then fix in cost order:** zero-result handling + synonyms → recall (index completeness, tokenization, filters) → ranking signals → semantic retrieval last. Adding embeddings to a broken tokenizer or filter pipeline just produces confident nonsense. Finally, re-ask the same users on the same 50 queries — if nDCG rose and the perception didn't, you fixed the wrong bucket.

**What's blocking a real diagnosis:** the logs (or even 200 queries with their top-10 results), 10–20 verbatim complaints *with the query the user typed*, the engine/index stack, and whether the complaint is uniform or localized to one language/locale. That last one matters most: if it's localized, the cause is almost always data or tokenization, not ranking.

If you need something before that instrumentation exists, there's a one-afternoon version: 20 queries, top 10 each, one line per bad result saying *why* — wrong entity, right topic wrong doc, right doc at rank 40, or no results. That's usually enough to pick the first fix.

Search relevance task — result. Workspace <SCRATCH>/tT10 was empty (no repo, no logs, no corpus), so I could not diagnose an actual cause and did not invent one. I wrote a diagnosis protocol + plan to `<SCRATCH>/tT10/search-relevance-diagnosis.md`.

Core point: "results feel irrelevant" is a perception, not a measurable. Diagnosing it requires three things that were absent — the queries users typed, the result sets they were shown, and the retrieval stack. Any specific cause stated without those would be fabrication.

Plan (cheapest-information first):
0. Freeze a judgment set: 50–100 stratified real queries, graded 0–3 by 2–3 raters, including the complainers. Without it every later change is unfalsifiable.
1. Slice logs before touching the ranker: zero-result rate, reformulation rate (<30s, strongest "results were wrong" signal), abandonment, CTR-by-position (flat CTR = presentation problem, not relevance), query/doc vocabulary overlap. Usually one bucket holds 60–80% of complaints.
2. Discriminate the five failure modes with one test each: query understanding (re-run with hand-normalized query), recall (is the known-good doc in the index / in candidates pre-ranking), ranking (median rank of known-good items), presentation (same results, better snippets/facets — does the complaint persist), coverage (zero-result clusters vs. inventory). Presentation is often the cheapest fix and the biggest perceived gain — check before buying a ranker.
3. Baseline nDCG@10 + MRR + zero-result rate on the frozen set, held-out only.
4. Fix in cost order: zero-result + synonyms/normalization → recall (index completeness, tokenization, filters) → ranking signals → semantic/hybrid last. Embeddings on a broken tokenizer/filter pipeline produce confident nonsense.
5. Re-ask the same users on the same 50 queries. If nDCG rose and perception didn't, the wrong bucket was fixed.

Fast path if a result is needed today: 20 queries, one person, top-10 each, one line per bad result saying why (wrong entity / right topic wrong doc / right doc at rank 40 / no results). One afternoon usually reveals the dominant mode.

Blocked on: search logs or ~200 queries with top-10 results; 10–20 verbatim complaints *with the query typed*; engine/index stack; corpus shape; whether the complaint is uniform or segment-specific (if localized to a language/locale, it's data or tokenization, not ranking). Assumptions recorded in the doc: document/keyword search rather than e-commerce personalization, complaints from live users, no semantic layer yet.
